# Study roadmap

[English](ROADMAP.md) · [中文](ROADMAP.zh.md)

Four study orders over the same pages, one per track of the hiring process described in the [hiring process guide](PROCESS.md). Pick the track that matches the role you are interviewing for and work down it. ★ shows how often a question comes up, from ★★★★★ (again and again) to ★☆☆☆☆ (rarely).

## Software engineering (SWE / Infra)

Product and infrastructure software engineers: online assessment, recruiter screen, a coding or system-design screen, then an onsite with coding, system design, project deep dive, culture and hiring manager.

### 1 · Before the first call

The recruiter screen already asks why Anthropic and what AI safety means to you, and many rejected candidates believed the culture round decided against them. Start both first; good answers take longer to prepare than code.

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Recruiter Screen: Motivation, Mission and Logistics](behavioral/recruiter-screen/README.md) | ★★★★★ | — | A 30-minute call with a recruiter, not an engineer, that opens on why you want to work at Anthropic and gives AI safety and Anthropic's mission a substantial share of the time at first-conversation depth, before covering your background and the logistics of the rest of the process: work authorization, timeline, compensation, and team fit. |
| 2 | [Culture Round: AI Safety, Values and Judgment](behavioral/culture-ai-safety/README.md) | ★★★★★ | — | A 55-minute onsite conversation about AI-safety judgment: why Anthropic and why safety matters to you, a chain of hypothetical dilemmas pressed with follow-ups, a critical read of the company's own published safety commitments, personal stories about being persuaded, repairing a relationship, and owning a mistake, and a separate read on your character and judgment through lighter, more personal prompts. |

### 2 · Core coding

The five most frequent coding problems. Four of them end in a follow-up on concurrency, I/O versus CPU, or durability, which is where most of the time goes.

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Image Processing Pipeline](coding/image-processing-pipeline/README.md) | ★★★★★ | Medium | Apply a JSON pipeline of Pillow transformations — grayscale, flip, scale, blur, rotate — to every image in a folder with exact rounding and resampling rules; then parallelise the batch across a process pool without re-decoding a source image once per pipeline; then reuse the leading steps two pipelines on the same image share, so each distinct prefix is computed exactly once. |
| 2 | [File Deduplication](coding/file-deduplication/README.md) | ★★★★★ | Medium | Walk a directory tree and group the files whose contents are byte-identical; then make the search efficient on large trees with a size, prefix-hash and full-hash filter; then parallelise the hashing so the concurrent result matches the sequential one exactly. |
| 3 | [Call Stacks from Profiler Samples](coding/stack-trace-reconstruction/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | Convert timestamped call-stack samples from a profiler into function start/end events using the longest common prefix between consecutive samples; then stream the same conversion in O(depth) memory with a debounce rule for noisy frames; then index known complete stack traces in a trie so a truncated crash trace can be matched against them by its trailing frames. |
| 4 | [Concurrent Web Crawler](coding/concurrent-web-crawler/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | Crawl every page reachable from a start URL under its hostname, given a slow, thread-safe get_urls helper: a single-threaded BFS first, then a bounded thread pool whose result and per-page fetch count must match it exactly, then an asyncio version bounded by a concurrency limit. |
| 5 | [Memoising LRU Cache: Bug Fix and Durability](coding/lru-cache-bugfix-durability/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | Fix three bugs in a functools.lru_cache-style memoising wrapper, centred on how positional and keyword arguments turn into a cache key; then make the cache survive a process crash with an append-only log and periodic snapshotting; then make it thread-safe, with single-flight so concurrent callers never compute the same missing key twice. |

### 3 · Core system design

Batched inference serving comes both as a blank-page design and as a flawed design document to review; weight distribution is the other frequent prompt.

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [LLM Inference API with Batched GPU Serving](system-design/inference-api-batching/README.md) | ★★★★★ | Hard | Design the public API and dispatcher in front of a pool of GPU model replicas that expose a fixed-latency batch call, covering batching policy, load balancing and admission control, KV-cache and prefix-cache arithmetic, real-time/offline isolation, and a follow-up scheduling policy for a large model that needs a whole 8-GPU pool against a small model that needs one GPU. |
| 2 | [Design Doc Review: A Batched Inference Service](system-design/design-doc-review/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Hard | Review a flawed design document for the batching and load-balancing layer in front of a GPU model-serving pool at 10,000 requests/second peak: rank the risks, correct a capacity estimate that silently assumes every batch is full, and fix the dispatch policy the document proposes for a shared 8-GPU pool serving a large and a small model. |
| 3 | [Distributing Model Weights to a GPU Fleet](system-design/model-weight-distribution/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Hard | Design the fastest way to get a several-hundred-GB checkpoint from object storage onto every host in a GPU fleet: derive the bandwidth lower bound, evolve from a naive pull and tree broadcast to a chunked peer-to-peer swarm, and handle integrity, versioning, stragglers and failures, and rate limiting against live serving traffic. |

### 4 · Online assessment

Practise under the real conditions — 90 minutes, four levels, each unlocked only once the previous one passes its tests — and keep the code extensible from the first level.

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Online Assessment: In-Memory Database](coding/oa-in-memory-database/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Medium | A four-level, gated online assessment: an in-memory store of (key, field) -> value records, extended level by level with sorted scans, per-field TTL expiry, and a backup/restore mechanism whose TTLs resume counting down from the moment of the restore. |
| 2 | [Online Assessment: Banking System](coding/oa-bank-system/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Medium | Build a bank-account class across four gated levels: deposits and withdrawals with exact return values, a leaderboard ranked by outgoing spend, a two-step transfer that holds funds until the recipient accepts or the hold expires, and an account merge whose effects a later point-in-time balance query must report correctly, including for an account id that is merged away and reused. |
| 3 | [Online Assessment: Recipe Manager](coding/oa-recipe-manager/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Medium | Build a recipe store across four gated levels: CRUD with case-insensitive name uniqueness, listings and search sorted by ingredient count with a stated tie-break, an owner-and-editor permission system that gates every edit and delete, and a version history whose rollback appends rather than truncates and never touches who owns or may edit a recipe. |

### 5 · More coding

Includes the AI-assisted rounds, where the assistant is allowed and the skill is reading, reviewing and verifying code quickly.

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Distributed Mode, Median and Sort](coding/distributed-mode-median/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Medium | Ten ranks each hold a shard of a large integer dataset and can only talk through send/recv/barrier. Compute the global mode with a hash-partitioned shuffle, the global median with a distributed binary search over the value range, and a full distributed sort, minimizing bytes moved across the network rather than bytes read locally. |
| 2 | [Reviewing and Improving Pull Requests with an AI Coding Assistant](coding/agentic-pr-review/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Medium | Review four open pull requests against a small Python job-queue library — the problem each solves, the specific problems in its diff, missing tests, and whether it can be merged — then choose one, improve it, add tests, and rewrite its description. |
| 3 | [Longest-Match Tokenizer](coding/longest-match-tokenizer/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Medium | Tokenize a string against a vocabulary by greedy longest match from the left, falling back to a per-character UNK id where nothing matches. Merge consecutive UNKs and bound the match search by the vocabulary's longest entry, then replace that search with a trie built once and reused across many texts. |
| 4 | [Building an Agent Loop with Tool Use](coding/llm-agent-tool-loop/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | Fix a buggy single-tool-call agent built on a Messages-API-style client, generalize it into a loop that answers questions needing several dependent lookups with a turn limit and error handling, then cut the number of model calls a fixed question set needs by parallelizing and batching tool calls. |
| 5 | [Boot Program Simulator: Find and Fix the Loop](coding/bootloader-loop-fix/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Medium | Simulate a tiny boot program of plus/next/jump instructions, detect the infinite loop that one corrupted instruction causes, then locate and repair that single instruction — first by trying every possible fix, then in linear time with a reverse-reachability graph. |

### 6 · More system design

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [One-to-One Chat System](system-design/one-on-one-chat/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | Direct messaging between exactly two users, online or offline: WebSocket delivery with at-least-once semantics and client-side deduplication, a durable per-recipient offline queue drained on reconnect, presence from heartbeats and a TTL key, and the Kafka-vs-Redis trade-off for the delivery bus behind a database that stays the source of truth. |
| 2 | [Prompt Playground (Product and Data Design)](system-design/prompt-playground/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | Design the product behind a prompt-engineering playground on top of a fixed browser/server/database deployment: the schema and API for prompts, immutable versions and runs, sharing with role-based permissions, and how very large prompts, concurrent edits and cost control are handled. |
| 3 | [Telemetry Pipeline with Schema Evolution](system-design/telemetry-data-infrastructure/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Hard | A fleet of deployed clients streams telemetry events into a pipeline that buffers, deduplicates, and stores them raw and curated for dashboards, ad hoc queries, and alerting under field-level access control; a schema registry and canonical-name mapping table fold already-deployed old clients' inconsistent telemetry_name variants into one metric without losing history or merging unrelated ones. |

### 7 · The rest of the onsite

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Project Deep Dive: Presentation and Technical Q&A](behavioral/project-deep-dive/README.md) | ★★★★★ | — | Present one past technical project of your choice for about 20-25 minutes, then defend it through 25-30 minutes of Q&A on context, architecture, rejected alternatives, your own contribution, results, failures, and scale. |
| 2 | [Hiring Manager Round: Impact, Collaboration and Growth](behavioral/hiring-manager/README.md) | ★★★★★ | — | A 45-to-55-minute conversation with the hiring manager about how you work: your most impactful project and your own role in it, how you prioritize and own outcomes when plans compete for the same time, cross-functional collaboration and disagreement, mentoring others and your own growth, and fit with the team, closing with the questions you put to the manager. |

### 8 · Other assessments

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Online Assessment: Task Manager with Expiry and Snapshots](coding/oa-task-manager/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Medium | A four-level, gated online assessment: per-user task CRUD with a stated sort order, extended with a per-task TTL that expires tasks lazily, and finished with a time-travel query that reconstructs a user's task list exactly as it stood at any past moment. |
| 2 | [Online Assessment: In-Memory File System](coding/oa-file-system/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Medium | Implement an in-memory, path-based file system across four levels: create, read and list files and directories; move, copy and delete them with exact overwrite semantics; add per-user storage quotas; and add point-in-time snapshots of the whole file system. |
| 3 | [Online Assessment: Cloud File Storage](coding/oa-cloud-storage/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Medium | Build a cloud storage class over four levels that each unlock once the previous one's tests pass: named files with sizes and copies; prefix/suffix search across the store; per-user accounts with storage quotas; and file compression paired with per-user backup and restore. |
| 4 | [Online Assessment: Office Access, Promotions and Pay](coding/oa-worker-grant-management/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Medium | Build a workforce-tracking class across four gated levels: office sessions from clock-in/clock-out events, a total-time leaderboard, promotions that take effect only at a worker's next entry, and pay calculated over sessions that may straddle a double-pay period, with overlapping bonus windows merged before the multiplier is applied. |

### 1 · Recruiter screen and culture

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Recruiter Screen: Motivation, Mission and Logistics](behavioral/recruiter-screen/README.md) | ★★★★★ | — | A 30-minute call with a recruiter, not an engineer, that opens on why you want to work at Anthropic and gives AI safety and Anthropic's mission a substantial share of the time at first-conversation depth, before covering your background and the logistics of the rest of the process: work authorization, timeline, compensation, and team fit. |
| 2 | [Culture Round: AI Safety, Values and Judgment](behavioral/culture-ai-safety/README.md) | ★★★★★ | — | A 55-minute onsite conversation about AI-safety judgment: why Anthropic and why safety matters to you, a chain of hypothetical dilemmas pressed with follow-ups, a critical read of the company's own published safety commitments, personal stories about being persuaded, repairing a relationship, and owning a mistake, and a separate read on your character and judgment through lighter, more personal prompts. |

### 2 · Research-track screens

The first technical round is one of these formats. Ask your recruiter which one you will get and prepare it first, then the others.

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Building an Agent Loop with Tool Use](coding/llm-agent-tool-loop/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | Fix a buggy single-tool-call agent built on a Messages-API-style client, generalize it into a loop that answers questions needing several dependent lookups with a turn limit and error handling, then cut the number of model calls a fixed question set needs by parallelizing and batching tool calls. |
| 2 | [Weighted Data Batcher with Checkpointing](coding/weighted-data-batcher/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Hard | Build a DataBatcher that draws each batch from several named datasets in proportion to integer weights, checkpoints and resumes so a paused run continues with byte-identical batches, and handles batch sizes that do not divide evenly across the weights. |
| 3 | [Prompting and Engineering with LLMs: Structured Output and Evaluation](coding/prompting-with-llms/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Medium | Design a system prompt and a robust parser that turns a language model's reply into a validated support-ticket label, find four bugs in a given evaluation pipeline, then use error analysis and a paired comparison to decide whether a prompt change is a real improvement or noise. |
| 4 | [ML Experiment Configuration System](coding/ml-config-system/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Hard | Configs are named nested dicts in an in-memory store. Compose them through bases with a deep merge and a delete marker, apply typed command-line overrides and interpolation, validate the result against a dataclass schema collecting every error, then freeze it and hash it for reruns. |
| 5 | [Multi-Head Attention with einsum](coding/qkv-attention-einsum/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Hard | Implement scaled dot-product attention and causal multi-head self-attention in NumPy using np.einsum for every contraction, then find and fix four planted bugs in a NumPy layer normalization plus attention block. |
| 6 | [Debugging a GRPO Training Loop](coding/grpo-debug/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Hard | Debug a small GRPO trainer in PyTorch that samples a group of completions per prompt on a toy verifiable-reward task, then defend the ratio, the clipping, and the group-normalized advantage that make it work. |

### 3 · Take-homes

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Take-Home: A Four-Hour Exploratory ML Study](take-home/ml-take-home/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Hard | A self-contained 4-hour take-home: implement a small classifier, then run a grid over symmetric label noise, training-set size, and hidden-layer width on synthetic data to see whether early stopping against a clean validation set recovers the accuracy the noise destroys. |
| 2 | [Take-Home: Sample-Wise Double Descent](take-home/interp-double-descent/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | Hard | A linear model's test error, plotted against the number of training samples n at a fixed model size, rises to a peak near the interpolation threshold and falls again on both sides. Reproduce the curve, explain the peak from the design matrix's singular values, and remove it with ridge. |

## Performance engineering

Performance engineers: a take-home or a coding screen instead of the assessment, then an onsite with performance modelling, systems design framed around performance bounds, and the conversation rounds.

### 1 · Take-home

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Take-Home: Optimising a Kernel on a Simulated Vector Machine](take-home/performance-kernel-optimization/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Hard | A from-scratch simulated vector processor — scalar and vector registers, packed instruction bundles, a load latency — comes with a naive kernel to speed up. The job is to pack, hoist, vectorise, unroll and software-pipeline it, checking each step's cycle count against a lower bound derived from the machine's own per-unit throughput. |

### 2 · Onsite technical rounds

Say which bound applies before doing arithmetic, and derive limits from first principles before proposing a design.

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Performance Modelling: Matmuls, Roofline and Sharding](coding/matmul-performance-modeling/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Hard | Estimate wall-clock time for bf16 matmuls of several shapes on one accelerator with a roofline model, extend it to a 72-layer stack of alternating matmuls and check whether it fits in one device's memory, compare pipeline and tensor parallelism across two devices on a single input, and build a cost model for sharding a feed-forward network by tensor or by token across p devices. |
| 2 | [Distributed Mode, Median and Sort](coding/distributed-mode-median/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Medium | Ten ranks each hold a shard of a large integer dataset and can only talk through send/recv/barrier. Compute the global mode with a hash-partitioned shuffle, the global median with a distributed binary search over the value range, and a full distributed sort, minimizing bytes moved across the network rather than bytes read locally. |
| 3 | [LLM Inference API with Batched GPU Serving](system-design/inference-api-batching/README.md) | ★★★★★ | Hard | Design the public API and dispatcher in front of a pool of GPU model replicas that expose a fixed-latency batch call, covering batching policy, load balancing and admission control, KV-cache and prefix-cache arithmetic, real-time/offline isolation, and a follow-up scheduling policy for a large model that needs a whole 8-GPU pool against a small model that needs one GPU. |
| 4 | [Distributing Model Weights to a GPU Fleet](system-design/model-weight-distribution/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Hard | Design the fastest way to get a several-hundred-GB checkpoint from object storage onto every host in a GPU fleet: derive the bandwidth lower bound, evolve from a naive pull and tree broadcast to a chunked peer-to-peer swarm, and handle integrity, versioning, stragglers and failures, and rate limiting against live serving traffic. |

## Anthropic Fellows

Applicants to the Anthropic Fellows Program: proctored assessments without AI or web search, interviews, then a research discussion.

### 1 · Assessments

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Online Assessment: DNS Resolver](coding/oa-dns-resolver/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | Medium | A five-level, gated online assessment: resolve names against a static in-memory DNS zone, extended level by level with CNAME-chain following and cycle detection, a fallback zone, a per-record TTL cache with lazy expiry, and thread-safe resolution that coalesces concurrent callers of the same name into one upstream lookup. |
| 2 | [Online Assessment: Banking System](coding/oa-bank-system/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Medium | Build a bank-account class across four gated levels: deposits and withdrawals with exact return values, a leaderboard ranked by outgoing spend, a two-step transfer that holds funds until the recipient accepts or the hold expires, and an account merge whose effects a later point-in-time balance query must report correctly, including for an account id that is merged away and reused. |
| 3 | [Online Assessment: Completing a Small LLM Inference Engine](coding/oa-inference-engine/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | Hard | Complete a small vLLM-style LLM serving engine across five gated levels, working from given, sparsely commented toy-model, block-allocator, sequence and request-queue code: admission and prefill, a budget-constrained decode scheduler, stop conditions and block freeing, hash-keyed prefix caching with LRU eviction, and preemption once the block pool runs out. |
